It                comprises a biodegradable polymer, and &#8815;                50 wt.% fugitive porogen material. The molar ratio                of soft segment block to hard segment block is                1:1.2-1:2.0.    USE - The melt-extrudable biodegradable ink is                useful for 3D printing; for fabricating graft; for                implanting the graft into a patient to heal or                augment a tympanic membrane or to replace a missing                tympanic membrane or missing portion; and for                implanting the graft into a patient to heal or                augment vasculature tissue, cartilage, a nerve                conduit, a tendon, muscle tissue, or a bone or to                replace a missing portion of vasculature tissue,                cartilage, nerve conduit, tendon, muscle tissue, or                bone (all claimed).    ADVANTAGE - The methods allow for rapid customization of                the 3D printed tissue graft. Specifically, due to                the nature of the new inks, and the melt-extrusion                temperature being slightly above the melting                temperature, 3D printed ink filaments solidify                rapidly. Thus, structures can be printed at high                aspect ratios (for example, up to 1:20 ratio                between the base:height of the portion) and high                resolution. Because the ink solidifies quickly                after being printed, it may be that the polymer                chains lock in their elongation created by shear                forces in the nozzle. This causes grafts to be                stiffer along the print path and cells to align,                even on topographically flat surfaces. The methods                achieve relevant mechanical properties for soft                tissue repairs and have good surgical handling.                Materials produced by the methods have a Young's                modulus of 5-500 MPa, e.g., 10-400 MPa, 20-250 MPa,                30-100 MPa (tunable with PEG addition and print                parameters), which is very close to living tissues.                The printed devices also have good structural                integrity, even when thin 50-100 &#956; m                devices such as grafts or implants are flexed and                manipulated through small cavities. The new methods                and devices also provide relevant in vivo                degradation rates and tissue adhesion/integration.                The degradation half-life of the printed devices                can be between about 1 and 12 months, e.g.,about                1-6 months, or about 1-3 months, depending on the                material and the specific use. A shorter                degradation half- life may be preferable to longer                degradation half-lives of implant materials that                are not intended to remain permanently in the body.                Additionally, the materials promote cellular                in-growth and angiogenesis, likely through the                urethane and urea bonds that resemble peptide bonds                for cells to form formal adhesions. m inner diameter nozzle, from a heated                extrusion print head;    implanting the graft into a patient to heal or                augment a tympanic membrane or to replace a missing                tympanic membrane or missing portion, which                involves accessing the damaged or missing tympanic                membrane (e.g. through a bilayer design or handle                on the graft); obtaining an appropriately sized and                configured graft in the form of an artificial                tympanic membrane device; and securing the                artificial tympanic membrane device to seal the                damaged portion of the tympanic membrane or                replacing the missing tympanic membrane or missing                portion; The                traction machine pulls and controls the wire                diameter to prepare with with diameter of                1.75&#177; 0.05 mm. The outer wall of the model                is printed with the wire and the inside of the                model is printed with water-soluble poly(vinyl                alcohol) (PVA) wire. The model has 2-6 holes with a                diameter of 0.2-0.6 cm. The photocatalyst in an                amount of 0.4-1.5 wt.% is dispersed ultrasonically                in isopropanol, where the photocatalyst and                isopropanol are used in volume ratio of less than                1:1 to 1:10. The resultant is then naturally cooled                down and then placed into an oven at                130-170&#176; C for heat treatment for 5-30                minutes. The device is placed into deionized water                for 1 hour and then washed with deionized water 4-6                times to remove the water-soluble PVA filling layer                and the weak catalyst on the surface. The device is                then dried in an oven at 60-80&#176; C. The                obtained wire is melted and the hole is blocked to                obtain a 3D printed self-suspension photocatalytic                device with a hollow structure. The bead of thermoplastic material is                extruded from an extrusion head. The tool path is                preheated (1006) by moving the laser image along                the tool path ahead of the extrusion head to                selectively irradiate the thermoplastic material of                partially printed element with a field of light                energy with a power intensity sufficient to heat                the thermoplastic material irradiated by the laser                image to a temperature at or above a                material-specific bonding temperature and below a                degradation temperature of the thermoplastic                material forming the previously-printed beads. USE - Method for additive manufacturing element in                fused deposition modeling three dimensional (3D)                printer. The better contact                between layers and greater diffusion are                achieved. DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Preparing zinc-magnesium alloy products by 3D                gel printing involves using 15.5-48.5 wt.%                magnesium, and balance is zinc (Zn) as raw                materials and dissolving 0.5-2.5 wt.% of zinc                naphthenate in organic solvent A, adding uniformly                mixed zinc powder and magnesium powder, stirring                and dispersing, and vacuum drying at                40-50&#176; C to obtain zinc-magnesium mixed                powder. The slurry is loaded into the barrel of the 3D gel                printer, and imported the shape of the product to                be printed into the computer control system for                printing. The diameter of the nozzle selected for                printing is 0.1-1.0mm, and the slurry passes                through The viscosity of the nozzle is 14-32                Pascals second, the printing layer height is                0.08-0.8mm, the extrusion rate is 50-200mm3/minute,                and the printing speed is 5-10mm/second. The spray                device sprays a mist of initiator benzoyl peroxide                (BPO) and catalyst                N,N,N',N'-tetramethylethylenediamine (TEMED) on the                printing surface. The printed body is dried in                vacuum at 30-50&#176; C for 8-24 hours, and                degrease the dried body at 100-400&#176; C in a                protective atmosphere for 5-10 hours and sintering                is carried out at 420-520&#176; C in a                protective atmosphere or a vacuum for 1-2 hours,                and the temperature is lowered to 350-380&#176;                C for 6-8 hours to obtain zinc-magnesium alloy                products.  US2023021383-A1	Forming biocompatible scaffold, useful to treat            tissue defect, comprises encapsulating agent in            microspheres, combining with matrix material, heating            in first cartridge of a device, dispensing through            printing needle, and forming scaffold	LEE C H	UNIV COLUMBIA NEW YORK (UYCO-C);  UNIV COLUMBIA NEW YORK (UYCO-C)	2016640447	   NOVELTY - Method (M1) for forming a biocompatible                scaffold, comprises: (a) encapsulating at least one                agent in many microspheres; (b) combining the                microspheres and a matrix material being suitable                for forming a scaffold via 3-dimensional (3D)                printing; (c) introducing the combination of                microspheres and matrix material into a first                cartridge of a 3D printing device; (d) heating; (e)                dispensing heated combination of microspheres and                matrix material through a printing needle to form a                polymeric microfiber; and (f) forming a scaffold                comprising many polymeric microfibers.    USE - The method is useful for forming a                biocompatible scaffold, which is useful for                treating a tissue defect, which is associated with                a multi-tissue interface comprising musculoskeletal                system, craniofacial system, periodontium, cementum                (CM)-periodontal ligament (PDL)-alveolar bone (AB)                complex, ligament-to-bone insertion, tendon-to-bone                insertion, rotator cuff, supraspinatus                tendon-to-bone interface, interface between tendon,                fibrocartilage, or bone, supraspinatus                tendon-fibrocartilage-bone interface, articular                cartilage-to-bone junction, anterior cruciate                ligament (ACL)-to-bone complex, anterior cruciate                ligament-fibrocartilage-bone interface,                intervertebral disc, nucleus pulposus-annulus                fibrosus-endplates, cementum-periodontal                ligament-alveolar bone, muscle-to-tendon,                inhomogeneous or anisotropic tissues, knee                meniscus, temporomandibular joint disc,                periodontium, root-periodontium complex, synovial                joints or fibrocartilaginous tissues (all claimed).                Test details are described but no results                given.    ADVANTAGE - The method: substantially maintains                bioactivity of encapsulated growth factors; results                in the formation of a multi-tissue complex, where                the mechanical properties or composition of the                resulting regenerated multi-tissue complex have                substantially similar mechanical properties or                composition of a corresponding native multi-tissue                complex; provides scaffold i.e. biocompatible                (claimed); utilizes 3D-printing delivery system                with micron precision and high spatial and temporal                resolution; and provides scaffold that has fully                integrated microchannels, mechanical stability                supporting initial loadbearing, growth factor                delivery (e.g. via microspheres) to guide                regeneration by (e.g. endogenous) progenitor cells                (e.g. stem cells), and high spatial and temporal                resolution.    DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Method (M1) for forming a biocompatible                scaffold, comprises: (a) encapsulating at least one                agent in many microspheres; (b) combining the                microspheres and a matrix material being suitable                for forming a scaffold via 3-dimensional (3D)                printing; (c) introducing the combination of                microspheres and matrix material into a first                cartridge of a 3D printing device; (d) heating the                combination of microspheres and matrix material in                the first cartridge to allow dispensing of the                combination while preventing substantial                degradation of the microsphere or the agent                encapsulated in the microsphere; (e) dispensing the                heated combination of microspheres and matrix                material from the first cartridge through a                printing needle to form a polymeric microfiber,                where the microspheres are distributed through the                polymeric microfiber; and (f) forming a scaffold                comprising many polymeric microfibers, where the                microspheres are distributed through the scaffold                by way of the polymeric microfibers. INDEPENDENT                CLAIMS are also included for:    a method (M2) for forming a polymeric fiber                having a microencapsulated agent distributed in the                polymeric fiber, comprising the steps (a)-(e) as                above per se; and    a composition comprising a polymeric                microfiber produced by 3D printing, and many                microspheres encapsulating at least one agent,                where the microsphere encapsulated agent is                distributed through the polymeric microfiber. The Si-TaN nanocrystals are present                in a concentration gradient, providing a controlled                degradation rate that is lower at a surface                adjacent to a die stack than at an opposing                exterior surface. A three-dimensional (3D) stack of                memory dies is disposed on the biodegradable PCB                substrate. The stack comprises a heterogeneous                integration of at least two different memory types                selected from ReRAM dies, MRAM dies, and low-power                double data rate 5 (LPDDR5) dies. Vertical                interconnects provide electrical communication                within the 3D stack of memory dies, where the                vertical interconnects consist essentially of tin                (Sn) and comprise both BackEnd-of-Line (BEOL) tin                vias for intra-die connections and Through-Silicon                tin Vias (TSVs) for inter-die vertical                connections.    USE - Sustainable high-density mobile memory chip                used in an electronic device selected from a mobile                smartphone or tablet computer, an Internet of                Things (IoT) sensor module, and an AI accelerator                module comprising memory chips arranged in a                high-bandwidth memory (HBM) configuration (claimed)                for automotive and aerospace electronics, and                semiconductor manufacturing and materials supply                chain.    ADVANTAGE - The sustainable high-density mobile memory                chip offers better recyclability, and provides                inherent electromigration resistance, imparts the                necessary mechanical strength, thermal stability,                and dielectric properties for semiconductor                packaging, while ensuring controlled degradation at                the product's end-of-life, allows for adaptive                performance tuning, balancing speed,                non-volatility, and power consumption for specific                mobile applications. This holistic approach yields                a memory system that is not only high-performing                and scalable but also significantly reduces the                environmental footprint of mobile                electronics.    DETAILED DESCRIPTION - Sustainable high-density mobile memory chip                comprises a biodegradable printed circuit board                (PCB) substrate comprising a biopolymer matrix                reinforced with silicon-tantalum nitride (Si-TaN)                nanocrystals. The Si-TaN nanocrystals are present                in a concentration gradient, providing a controlled                degradation rate that is lower at a surface                adjacent to a die stack than at an opposing                exterior surface. A three-dimensional (3D) stack of                memory dies is disposed on the biodegradable PCB                substrate. The stack comprises a heterogeneous                integration of at least two different memory types                selected from resistive random-access memory                (ReRAM) dies, magnetoresistive RAM dies, and                low-power double data rate 5 (LPDDR5) dies.                Vertical interconnects provide electrical                communication within the 3D stack of memory dies,                where the vertical interconnects consist                essentially of tin (Sn) and comprise both                BackEnd-of-Line (BEOL) tin vias for intra-die                connections and Through-Silicon tin Vias (TSVs) for                inter-die vertical connections. A thermal interface                material (TIM) layer is disposed between at least                two components of the 3D stack. The TIM layer                comprises a composite of carbon nanoparticles, tin                micro/nano particles, and tin oxide (SnO2)                nanoparticles, where the (SnO2) nanoparticles form                a passivation layer around the tin micro/nano                particles to inhibit oxidation during                high-temperature operation.    INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are also included for the                following: (1) a biodegradable nanocomposite                material for a semiconductor package substrate; (2)                a tin-based thermal interface material for                semiconductor packaging; (3) a method for                manufacturing a sustainable high-density mobile                memory chip; (4) a method for recycling a mobile                memory chip, the chip comprising a 3D stack of                memory dies with tin-based interconnects mounted on                a biodegradable PCB substrate with a tin-based                thermal paste; (5) a method for operating a                sustainable high-density mobile memory chip to                optimize performance and power consumption, the                chip comprising a 3D heterogeneous stack of ReRAM,                MRAM, and LPDDR5 memory dies with tin-based                vertical interconnects on a biodegradable                substrate; and (6) a method for maintaining thermal                performance in a mobile memory chip, the chip                having a tin-based thermal interface material (TIM)                layer comprising carbon nanoparticles, tin                micro/nano particles, and tin oxide                nanoparticles. The                lower GelMA/&#946;-tricalcium phosphate                (TCP)/BP/Exo scaffold is prepared and printed, and                then the upper GelMA/BP/Exo scaffold is prepared                and printed to obtain the                GelMA/&#946;-TCP/BP/Exo dual layer composite                hydrogel scaffold, where the three-dimensional                hydrogel scaffold uses an extrusion 3D                printer. USE - System for drying filament e.g. plastic                filament used in additive manufacturing machine                (claimed) e.g. extrusion based additive                manufacturing (AM) machine such as extrusion                three-dimensional (3D) printer. DETAILED DESCRIPTION - The bone tissue engineering scaffold featuring                dual gradients of magnesium content and modulus,                comprises composite formed from an active                fiber-reinforced, enzyme-responsive degradable                hydrogel and a 3D-printed bioceramic scaffold.The                3D-printed bioceramic scaffold consists of                beta-tricalcium phosphate (&#946;-TCP) and                whitlockite (WH); hydrogel filling the pores with                the bioceramic scaffold is prepared via                photocrosslinking and chemical crosslinking using                methacrylated gelatin (GelMA), methacrylated                hyaluronic acid (HAMA), and thiol-terminated matrix                metalloproteinase (MMP)-sensitive peptide chains;                magnesium ion-loaded GelMA/HAMA composite fibers                are uniformly dispersed within the hydrogel, such                that magnesium ion content and modulus                progressively increase from the hydrogel matrix to                the fibers, and finally to bioceramic scaffold,                forming an organic-inorganic composite bone tissue                engineering scaffold possessing dual gradients of                both magnesium content and modulus. The preparation                process is as follows: (1) Preparation of WH                nanoparticles: Weigh specific amounts of calcium                hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide and add them to                100 mL of deionized water, wherein the amount of                calcium hydroxide added is 1.5 g to 2 g per 100 mL,                and the amount of magnesium hydroxide added is 0.7                g to 1 g; stir the mixture at 400 rpm in a 100                &#176;C oil bath for 30 minutes; subsequently,                add 100 mL of a 0.5 M aqueous phosphoric acid                solution to the flask; after reacting continuously                for 10 hours, allow the mixture to stand and age at                room temperature for 14 hours; wash with deionized                water, collect the precipitate via centrifugation,                and-after drying and grinding heat the material at                a ramp rate of 10 &#176;C/min up to 650                &#176;C, hold at this temperature for 3 hours,                and then cool it down to room temperature at a rate                of 10 &#176;C/min to complete the annealing                process, thereby obtaining the WH nanoparticles;                (2) Preparation of the &#946;-TCP/WH inorganic                scaffold. a. Mix the &#946;-TCP/WH powder with                a polymeric binder, and utilize 3D printing                technology to fabricate a three-dimensional                scaffold possessing the desired porous structure                and stiffness; b. Subject the three-dimensional                scaffold to post-processing, including drying to                remove moisture and sintering to eliminate the                binder, thereby obtaining a &#946;-TCP/WH                inorganic scaffold; (3) Preparation of active                fiber-reinforced, MMP-responsive hydrogels: a.                Preparation of the spinning solution: Dissolve                MgCl2 in deionized water; dissolve GelMA, HAMA, and                the photoinitiator lithium                phenyl(2,4,6-trimethylbenzoyl)phosphinate (LAP) in                aqueous solution of tetrahydrofuran; subsequently,                mix the two solutions thoroughly to obtain the                spinning solution; b. Preparation of the fibrous                membrane: Transfer the solution prepared in step                (a) into a syringe pump for electrospinning, using                aluminum foil to collect the fibers; c. Dry the                collected fibrous membrane in vacuum oven at a                temperature not exceeding 40 &#176;C until a                constant weight is achieved, followed by UV                irradiation for 5 minutes; subsequently, place                fibrous membrane in tert-butanol, homogenize to                disperse the fibers, and then freeze-dry the                mixture to obtain dispersed active fibers; d.                Preparation of pre-gel solution: Dissolve GelMA and                HAMA in a phosphate-buffered solution, and add the                photoinitiator LAP, a crosslinking MMP-sensitive                peptide sequence, and dispersed active fibers                prepared in step (c) to the solution; e. Active                fiber-reinforced hydrogel: Place pre-gel solution                into a mold and allow it to stand at 37 &#176;C                for 1 hour to undergo crosslinking, followed by UV                irradiation for 1 minute, and obtaining active                fiber-reinforced, MMP-responsive, and degradable                hydrogel; (4) Preparation of a composite scaffold                featuring dual gradients in magnesium content and                modulus. a. Preparation of pre-gel solution:                Dissolve GelMA and HAMA in deionized water, and add                photoinitiator LAP, crosslinking agent                (MMP-sensitive peptide chain), and active                reinforcing fibers to the mixture; b. Infiltration                and gelation of the pre-gel solution: Infiltrate                the solution prepared in step (a) into the pores of                a 3D-printed &#946;-TCP/WH scaffold; allow it                to stand at 37 &#176;C for 1 hour to crosslink,                followed by 1 minute of UV irradiation treatment,                thereby obtaining an organic-inorganic gradient                composite scaffold featuring dual gradients in both                magnesium content and modulus. The                nano-crystalline metal organic framework is                homogeneously dispersed and present only within the                mesopores or void spaces of the mesoporous                polymeric material.    USE - Manufacture of metal organic framework                suspension such as colloidal suspension, colloidal                ink and ink used as polymeric additive for forming                polymeric membrane (claimed). Can also be used for                coating, film, textile, food packaging and gas and                liquid chromatography and chiral chromatography for                sensing, capturing and catalytic degradation of                harmful gases and vapor, personal protection, ink                for 3D printing, electronics, photoluminescent,                sensor, optoelectronics and drug delivery.    ADVANTAGE - The method enables the effective manufacture                of metal organic framework suspension having                excellent quality and effectively suppresses the                formation of pinholes on membrane during                application and provides the membrane having                excellent permeability and selectivity.  EP4411114-A2;  EP4411114-A3;  US12421859-B2;  EP4411114-B1	Additively manufacturing or three dimensional            printing metal-plated fiber-reinforced plastic seal            plate such as cabin air compressor seal plate, for            rotary machine for use in gas turbine engine            applications, has metal plating arranged on portion of            outer surface of plastic substrate	KILCHYK V;  MERRITT B J	HAMILTON SUNDSTRAND CORP (SUNH-C);  HAMILTON SUNDSTRAND CORP (SUNH-C)	2024823316	   NOVELTY - The seal plate (124) has a hub included with a                bore centered on a central axis of the rotary                machine. A disk portion (122) extends radially                outwards from the hub, where the hub and the disk                portion together comprises a plastic substrate. The                plastic substrate is included with a matrix                material. Fibers are embedded in the matrix                material. The fibers having a first coefficient of                thermal expansion. A metal plating is arranged on                portion of an outer surface of the plastic                substrate. The metal plating having a second                coefficient of thermal expansion of the metal                plating, where bulk coefficient of thermal                expansion of the plastic substrate at the outer                surface of the plastic substrate substantially                matches the second coefficient of thermal expansion                of the metal plating.    USE - Additively manufacturing or three dimensional                (3D) printing metal-plated fiber-reinforced plastic                seal plate such as cabin air compressor seal plate,                for rotary machine for use in gas turbine engine                applications.    ADVANTAGE - The metal-plated plastic seal plate components                with controlled thermal expansion behavior have an                increased durability in environments of varying                temperature or temperature gradients. The                metal-plated components include reduced weight,                reduced costs, and faster design, manufacturing,                and testing time. The metal plating is positioned                on the entirety of or portions of outer surface to                help increase strength and reduce degradation of                seal plate from abrasives moving through                turbomachine. The first region and second region of                fiber-reinforced plastic structure are areas of                increased fiber density that aid in reducing and                preventing deflection of seal plate, thus reducing                clearances in turbomachine and increasing                efficiency. The third region of fiber-reinforced                plastic structure is an area of increased fiber                density that aids in stress reduction during                operation of turbomachine to reduce the stress in                third region of seal plate. The stresses at stress                regions reduce the failure rate of seal plate as                well as the failure rate of turbomachine.    DETAILED DESCRIPTION - An INDEPENDENT CLAIM is included for a method                for forming a seal plate for a rotary                machine.  SURESH B R;  RAJANBABU T;  SUDHAKAR S;  SELVARAJ V	INDIAN INST TECHNOLOGY MADRAS (IITM-C)	202576018D	   NOVELTY - The bio-ceramic hydrogel composite comprises a                polymeric hydrogel scaffold comprising a first                polymer and a second polymer, and a calcium-based                bio-ceramic doped with a multiple of metal ions to                form an ion-doped bio-ceramic, where the multiple                of metal ions comprises zinc ions, copper ions, and                strontium ions, and where the ion-doped bio-ceramic                is embedded within the polymeric hydrogel                scaffold.    USE - Bio-ceramic hydrogel composite for tissue                regeneration (claimed), i.e., for treating and/or                regenerating tissue, where the tissue is preferably                selected from vascular tissue, and/or bone                tissue.    ADVANTAGE - The composite addresses challenge in bone and                vascular tissue engineering by combining the                osteogenic properties of ion-doped bio-ceramics                with the structural support of a polymeric hydrogel                scaffold. The composite addresses critical                limitations in conventional bone regeneration                therapies, such as poor osteointegration,                inadequate mechanical strength, and the frequent                need for secondary surgical interventions. By                developing a novel bio-ceramic hydrogel composite,                the composite offers a multifunctional solution                that enhances both biological and mechanical                performance in bone tissue engineering. The                bio-ceramic hydrogel composite prepared in                accordance with the composite, comprises ion-doped                hydroxyapatite (HAp), synthesized and doped with                zinc (Zn2+), copper (Cu2+), and strontium (Sr2+) to                form triple iondoped HAp (HApTi), which                collectively improve osteoconduction and                angiogenesis. These ions are strategically                incorporated into the HAp lattice to substitute                calcium or phosphate sites, enhancing bioactivity                while maintaining structural integrity. The doped                HAp (HApTi) serves as a bioactive phase that                promotes bone cell differentiation and                vascularization-key processes for effective tissue                regeneration. To support the bio-ceramic phase, the                invention utilizes a chitosan sodium alginate                matrix. This polymeric blend offers superior                mechanical stability compared to either polymer                alone, while maintaining excellent                biocompatibility, biodegradability, and tunable                mechanical properties. The matrix mimics the                extracellular environment, facilitating cell                attachment, proliferation, and nutrient exchange.                The composite was fabricated using both controlled                freeze-drying and 3D printing techniques, ensuring                precise architecture and mechanical robustness. The                structural and chemical characterization using SEM,                FTIR, and XRD confirmed the successful integration                of components and the formation of a stable                composite. The chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) assay                in chick embryos demonstrated high vascularization                potential. Zebrafish models-including hatching                rate, viability, scale regeneration, vertebral                staining, and tail fracture studies-confirmed the                scaffold's osteoinductive and regenerative                capabilities. Furthermore, in vivo implantation in                a rat tibial defect model showed significant bone                formation, supporting the scaffold's translational                potential for clinical applications. The composite                provides a robust, bioactive, and mechanically                stable scaffold that supports bone regeneration                through ion-driven bioactivity, structural support,                and controlled degradation. It lays a strong                foundation for future applications in regenerative                medicine, offering a promising alternative to                traditional bone repair strategies.    DETAILED DESCRIPTION - INDEPENDENT CLAIMS are included for: (1) a                bio-ceramic hydrogel composite composition for                forming the bio-ceramic hydrogel composite, which                comprises the ion-doped bio-ceramic, and a first                polymer and a second polymer;    (2) a process of preparing a bio-ceramic                hydrogel composite, which involves preparing a                first solution comprising the calcium-based                bio-ceramic and the multiple of metal ions                comprising zinc ions, copper ions, and strontium                ions, preparing a second solution comprising the                first polymer and a second polymer, mixing the                first solution with the second solution to obtain a                reaction mixture, and crosslinking to allow                formation of the bio-ceramic hydrogel composite;                and    (3) a method for tissue regeneration, which                involves providing the bio-ceramic hydrogel                composite at a target site.
